title: Increasing Energy Efficiency of Astrophysics Simulations Through GPU Frequency Scaling
problem: GPU-accelerated HPC simulations consume substantial energy but lack kernel-level energy optimization strategies. Existing system-level monitoring provides insufficient granularity for detailed GPU energy consumption analysis needed to optimize individual computational workloads.
motivation: Escalating energy consumption in HPC centers conflicts with stricter environmental regulations and sustainability goals, requiring workload-specific energy efficiency improvements for GPU-based systems.
method: The authors instrumented SPH-EXA, an open-source GPU-centric astrophysical simulation framework, with a power/energy measurement toolkit supporting diverse CPU-GPU node architectures. They implemented dynamic GPU frequency scaling within computational kernels and benchmarked both static and dynamic frequency scaling strategies to characterize energy-performance trade-offs.
key_novelty: Kernel-level dynamic GPU frequency scaling for astrophysical simulations that achieves measurable energy reduction while maintaining acceptable performance within a production HPC framework.
contributions: Open-source power and energy measurement toolkit for CPU-GPU heterogeneous architectures with kernel-level granularity
Dynamic GPU frequency scaling mechanism enabling runtime frequency control at the computational kernel level
Empirical comparison of static versus dynamic frequency scaling strategies in astrophysical simulation workloads
Demonstration that dynamic frequency scaling reduces total energy consumption with limited performance degradation
limitations: Specific magnitudes of energy savings and performance trade-offs are not quantified; generalizability beyond astrophysical simulations is not discussed.
primary_theme: dynamic GPU frequency scaling for HPC sustainability
